lines.text: We fed them everything Greyhollow grew. Barley bread. Barley beer. Beans and cabbages from the glasshouses. In the north, at harvest's end, when every other hall was eating salt fish.
Then our serving girls brought in the boar. One girl. One boar. One hand.
That girl just carried a beast I'd need two men to lift.
She's strong for her age.
That girl lifts like a knight. Your stable boy lifts like a knight. Your whole village lifts like knights. That's a three, Lord Lucan, at the very least.
How fascinating. And how does Lord Lucan explain it?
Good soil.
Under the table, Ilse kicked me.
My lords. Lady Marrick. Corrow has closed the Senn to all of us. Your furs and your timber rot on the same docks as my glass.
So I propose a Compact. The Northern Compact. Three things.
One. We sell our rimeglass together, through Saltmouth, at a fair price. Two. Every house that signs gets shares in Saltmouth harbour. Three. When the Pale comes south, we stand together.
Shares in a harbour. How many?
Ten parts in a hundred for each house, my lady. Paid every quarter, in Greyhollow notes or in glass. Your choice.
Halvard Kesting laughed. Not politely. He laughed until the cups rattled.
Stand together! Against the Pale! I've held Kesting Pass for forty years, boy. I buried two sons in it. And you'll help me hold it with what? Turnips?
A Compact, written by a zero. Signed by a widow, a peacock, and an old bear. The south will laugh harder than I do.
Peacock?
Nobody else laughed. Not the lords. Not my people, standing there with the plates. The hall went very quiet.
Lord Kesting. Have you ever had a hot bath?
...A what?
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter fifty, coming soon.
